how.h: Meridian writes every step before sending it.
how.s1.p: A single “pay” call, whatever PSP sits behind it. Same reference, same result, even if the request is sent twice.
how.s2.p: Each step is recorded in a chained, signed journal before it reaches the PSP, with one idempotency key per step.
how.s3.h: The outcome is guaranteed and provable
how.s3.p: If anything drops, Meridian resumes from the journal and recovers the real outcome. Every payment ends with a verifiable proof.
guar.r1.b: Keeps the payment “in progress”, never “failed”, and queries the PSP
guar.r2.b: Replays with the same idempotency key
guar.r3.b: Another instance resumes from the shared journal
guar.r4.b: Fails over to the backup PSP, only if nothing was sent
guar.r5.b: Returns the real outcome and allows a refund

psp.title: Be in every till, without one more integration.
psp.lede: To reach a merchant you must be integrated into their till, vendor by vendor, country by country. Meridian gets you there in one go, without touching your customer relationship.

code.h: Five calls. The same code for every PSP.
code.p: Pay, check status, cancel, refund, get the receipt. The SDK handles retries, timeouts and lost responses. Switching PSP means changing a setting, not your code.
flow.n4: Backup, only if nothing was sent
flow.cap: A payment never leaves Meridian without being written to the journal. After an outage, recovery starts from the journal, not from a guess.
guar.stat: 0 double charges across 200 random failure sequences, on every release.
faq.1.a: No. Meridian is a technical provider: it holds no funds and signs no contracts with merchants. Payments are executed by the PSP the merchant chose, under its own licence.
faq.2.q: Does card data go through Meridian?
faq.2.a: No. The card is read by the terminal and processed by the PSP. Meridian only receives the result, the brand and the last 4 digits for the receipt.
faq.3.q: What happens if Meridian goes down?
faq.3.a: Several instances share the same journal. If one fails mid-payment, another resumes from the last written step and recovers the real outcome from the PSP. This scenario is tested on every release.
faq.4.q: Do my Concert or ZVT tills need to change?
faq.4.a: No. You point the till at Meridian instead of the terminal; the messages stay the same.
faq.5.a: Stripe Terminal, currently being validated on its sandbox. Each new PSP arrives as a declarative module, published after passing the eight failure scenarios.
faq.6.a: The vendor, through a subscription per active terminal, with no per-transaction fees. They can include it in their offer at their own price. The merchant pays Meridian nothing extra; their fees stay with their PSP.

st.1.p: The till calls Meridian. Before writing to the PSP, Meridian records the step in its journal.
st.2.p: An ordinary till shows “failed”. The customer pays again. The double charge is done.
st.3.p: The payment stays “in progress”. When the network returns, Meridian asks the PSP with the same key and recovers the real outcome.
st.4.p: The customer is charged once. The receipt prints, with its signed proof.
s3.p: Five calls. The same code, whatever the merchant's PSP. Switching PSP becomes a setting.
s4.p: Concert in France, ZVT in Germany, nexo everywhere. Point the till at Meridian; nothing else changes.
s5.h: Eight countries. The way they pay.
s5.p: Cards, and the payment methods each country actually uses.
s6.p: The PSP keeps the contract, KYC, funds and its fees. Meridian sees neither the card nor the money: only the result, and its proof.
s7.p: No sign-up. A real payment, a real outage, thirty seconds.
